content.text: Can we look for duplicate photos among the entered images in the db, and if the same image is entered, ask user if they want to remake the discovery (deleting the old one) before making the AI agent call?

Implemented client-side duplicate photo detection in IndexedDB using dual-stage verification: cryptographic SHA-256 hash for exact byte matches and perceptual difference hashing (dHash) for resized/re-encoded images. Added a pre-analysis interceptor in DiscoverClient to display a modal with the existing match and an automated remake flow that removes the prior discovery.
I have already discovered one specimen, but in number of discoveries it is unable to calculate the number of discoveries for a user on the profile page.

Identified that discoveries are stored locally on the user device in IndexedDB for privacy and zero cloud storage costs, while the profile was querying MongoDB discoveries count. Implemented ProfileAchievementsClient and /api/user/sync to dynamically read device IndexedDB discoveries upon hydration and synchronize the count and XP progression to the user cloud profile.
Fix the Vercel deployment failure in my existing EarthLens AI repository. Build log shows npm error ERESOLVE resolving vitest@5.0.3 and @types/node.

Diagnosed the peer dependency conflict: package.json specified @types/node@^20, but vitest@5.0.3 strictly requires @types/node@^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0 and vite@8.3.4 requires >=22.12.0. Aligned @types/node to ^22.12.0, specified engines.node >=22.12.0, and cleanly regenerated package-lock.json with standard npm install. Verified clean build and all 38 Vitest tests passed.
Once you have signed out you cannot use any of the features, do check this as it was still showing the journal even if the user is not logged in.

Implemented defense-in-depth security: Added Next.js Edge middleware (middleware.ts) protecting all feature routes (/discover, /journal, /insight, /studio, /profile) with JWT cookie verification. Wrapped JournalPage and InsightPage in protected server components that redirect unauthenticated visitors to /login, and added client-side session validation to immediate boot unauthenticated sessions.
Upon deployment it is showing Invalid Origin or Referer error when trying to log in.

Diagnosed CSRF validation error in lib/server/auth.ts: verifyCsrfOrigin was strictly checking against APP_BASE_URL (http://localhost:3000), which blocked requests coming from Vercel deployment domains (*.vercel.app). Upgraded verifyCsrfOrigin to dynamically validate x-forwarded-host, host, request URL host, and Vercel domains.
